sentences.text: The genus Franconiasaurus contains only one known species, F. brevispinus, which is known from two well-preserved three-dimensional skeletons.
These two specimens provide rare insight into the anatomy of this basal plesiosauroid plesiosaur from the Early Jurassic of Germany.
The genus name combines the region of Franconia with the Greek word for reptile, while the species name refers to the short neural spines found on some of its cervical and dorsal vertebrae.
Fossils were unearthed in the Mistelgau fossil pit located in the Bayreuth District of Bavaria, Germany.
The primary specimen, a nearly complete and partially articulated skeleton, was found between 2014 and 2018.
A second, incomplete and disarticulated specimen discovered in 2005 was also assigned to this genus.
Paleontologists Sachs, Eggmaier, and Madzia formally described Franconiasaurus brevispinus as a new genus and species in 2024.
Phylogenetic analyses place Franconiasaurus as a member of Plesiosauria that is the sister taxon to Cryptoclidia.
It is considered to fill an evolutionary gap between early plesiosauroids and later-diverging groups like cryptoclidids and elasmosaurids.
Franconiasaurus lived during the Early Jurassic period in Germany, specifically between 180.4 and 174.7 million years ago during the Toarcian stage.
